Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached are the contract redlines from our legal team and a short note on a key commercial ask from procurement. Two items we need Redwood to consider to proceed to exec review on our side:

1) Early opt-out window: Aurora is asking for a 60-day opt-out period from go-live where we can exit with a limited fee. Proposed: 30% of remaining committed fees if we opt out within first 60 days.
2) Ramp staircase / downsell protection: during the first 6 months we'd like a stepped ramp that guarantees a stepped capacity schedule with the option to reduce committed TUs by up to 40% on month 3 and month 6 with a smaller unwind payment.

Our procurement team indicated these are material commercial changes; please let us know if Redwood can offer an alternative structure (e.g., smaller unwind fee + service credits) so we can move to final sign-off. I’ve attached the redlines (PDF) and a short mutual action plan (docx).

Forwarding Aurora’s redlines — they are asking for a 60-day opt-out with a 30% unwind and the ability to downsize committed TUs by up to 40% at month 3 and month 6. This is outside our standard ramp protections.

My read: we can make a workable exception if we get the following controls:
- Reduce the opt-out unwind to 15% if exercised within first 60 days OR accept 30% but capped to the incremental committed dollars above actual usage (protects unit economics).
- Staged downsell allowed up to 25% on month 3 and an additional 15% on month 6 (cumulative 40%), but each step triggers a minimum reconfirmation period and reduced SLA (lower priority for burst capacity) for downsized tiers.
- Include a chargeback to cover onboarding and reserved GPU capacity (one-time transition fee).

Can you confirm whether you’re comfortable approving the 15% unwind + staged downsell (25% then 15%) as a standard exec exception? If not, I’ll propose the alternate (30% but capped) and we can request C-level approval. Also note we may need to offer a modest signing credit (5–7%) to keep ARR healthy.

—Marissa

Marissa / Priyom — thanks for the summary. I reviewed the commercial impact and am willing to approve an exception with the following strict conditions:

1) Opt-out unwind: allow a 60-day opt-out with a 15% unwind fee OR allow a 30% unwind but limited to the incremental committed dollars above the customer’s actual consumption during the period (whichever results in higher recovered economics for Redwood).
2) Staged downsell: permit up to 25% reduction at month 3 and an additional 15% at month 6 (max 40% cumulative) provided that each downsell triggers: a) a one-time transition fee equal to two weeks of committed spend for the downsized portion, and b) automatic downgrade to a reduced SLA tier for the downsized capacity (documented in SOW).
3) Sign-on credit: approve up to 5% one-time credit to be applied to the first invoice only.
4) Executive notification: legal and finance must sign off on the final contract language; the deal desk to include a route-to-credit that requires Finance approval for any future unwind under this clause.

I’m approving the above as an exec exception. Please update the redlines to reflect the 15%/capped-30% option, the transition fee language, and the SLA downgrade. Once redlines are in, Priyom please get legal review and send to Aurora with the updated MAP and DocuSign link.

Vivek
